AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preparing Animal Products? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Preparing Animal Products.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preparing Animal Products.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preparing Animal Products.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preparing Animal Products.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.

3. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Removing all vegetation

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growing Trees? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Trees.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growing Trees.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growing Trees.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Growing Trees.

5. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Decomposers only

7. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Constructing Water Retention Structures? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Constructing Water Retention Structures.

9. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Establishment Planting Site? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Establishment Planting Site.

11. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. newton (N)

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hygiene in Rearing Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hygiene in Rearing Animals.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hygiene in Rearing Animals.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hygiene in Rearing Animals.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Hygiene in Rearing Animals.

   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production .

14. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

15. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

16. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

17. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conserving Food Nutrients? (1 mark)

20. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Milk souring

21. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preparing Animal Products 9 2.4 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene? (1 mark)

   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preparing Animal Products 9 2.4 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene.

22. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking Food? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking Food.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking Food.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking Food.
